result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_dominating_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of nodes forms a dominating set. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L45445-L45534){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_dominating_set(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is dominating set](/assets/graphs/is-dominating-set.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same two-by-three ladder on both sides, with the candidate nodes outlined. Left: every node is B, E, or next to one of them, so is_dominating_set() returns True. Right: with B and D, node F (shown in the accent color) has no neighbor in the set, so is_dominating_set() returns False." width="100%"} A dominating set `D` of a graph `G = (V, E)` is a subset of V such that every vertex not in `D` is adjacent to at least one member of `D`. In other words, every node is either in `D` or has a neighbor in `D`. Dominating sets model coverage problems where each chosen node "serves" itself and its immediate neighbors. Use this method to check, for example, whether: - a set of facilities (hospitals, cell towers, warehouses) covers every location that is one hop away - a set of monitors or sensors observes every node in a network - the output of `dominating_set()` or `min_weighted_dominating_set()` is valid Node IDs in `nodes=` that don't exist in the graph are silently ignored, and duplicates are harmless. For directed graphs, a node outside the set counts as dominated only if it has an edge pointing *to* a member of the set (an out-neighbor in `D`); edges pointing from a member to it do not count. Convert with `to_undirected()` first if you want direction to be ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer node IDs forming the candidate dominating set. Labels are not accepted; use `get_id_from_label()` to convert them. An empty list is only a dominating set of an empty graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if every node in the graph is in `nodes=` or adjacent to a node in `nodes=`, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A dominating set covers every vertex either directly or via a neighbor, so validation is a single pass: every vertex outside the input set must have at least one neighbor inside it. The scan costs $O(V + E)$. Edge cases behave predictably: the empty set dominates only the empty graph, and the entire vertex set is always a dominating set (trivially). A single-node set dominates exactly that node and its neighborhood. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path `A-B-C-D`, the set `{B, D}` dominates the whole graph: `B` covers `A` and `C`, while `D` covers itself: ::: {#fd608178 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") d_id = graph.get_id_from_label("D") # Returns True graph.is_dominating_set([b_id, d_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Dropping `D` leaves it uncovered, since `B` alone doesn't reach that far: ::: {#044621ec .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False: D is neither in the set nor adjacent to a member graph.is_dominating_set([b_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: This is a convenient way to confirm a dominating set produced by `dominating_set()` is actually valid: ::: {#12c90f92 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_gnm_graph(n=50, m=100, seed=23) dom = graph.dominating_set() # Returns True: dominating_set() always produces a valid result graph.is_dominating_set(dom) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
